items.title: Taking Tokenization off the Host for Agentic LLM Serving
items.abstract: Agentic workloads resend long contexts that barely change between calls. Prefix caching now skips most of their prefill, yet every request must still be tokenized in full before the cache can even be consulted. Tokenization, a CPU stage long treated as negligible, becomes the largest part of time-to-first-token (TTFT), and a frontend that tokenizes for a whole GPU fleet limits how many GPUs it can feed. We present GraphTok, a GPU tokenizer that runs the entire encoding pipeline, from pre-tokenization through byte-pair encoding (BPE) merging to token-ID assembly, as one replayable CUDA graph. GraphTok reproduces the reference token IDs bit-for-bit on GPT-2, Llama 3, Qwen 2.5, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemma 3, hands short inputs to a CPU engine where the GPU cannot win, and plugs into unmodified vLLM and NVIDIA Dynamo. GraphTok encodes one million GPT-2 tokens in 1.7-3.2 ms including data transfers, and on Llama 3 it is 4.7-6.0x faster than gigatoken, the strongest CPU tokenizer. On TokTier's own single-request benchmark, it is 2.6-3.9x faster than gigatoken and up to 18.1x faster than TokTier. In vLLM with a cached prefix, it lowers mean TTFT by 2.1-2.4x. The largest gain is capacity. Within a 2 s P99 target, one Dynamo frontend with GraphTok sustains 518 requests/s of 121k-token traffic, the busiest-hour load of 56 GPUs, against 296 with gigatoken and 18.5 with the default tokenizer. Across 121k to one million tokens, this is 1.75-2.5x the load gigatoken sustains, with a P99 up to 64x lower where gigatoken's tail breaks.
items.summary_cn:
## 文章做了什么
- **背景**：随着 LLM 代理（Agentic）应用的兴起，工作负载呈现出长上下文重复调用的特点。虽然前缀缓存（Prefix Caching）技术已经能够跳过大部分预填充（Prefill）计算，但在查询缓存之前，每个请求仍然必须完整地进行分词（Tokenization）。
- **已有工作的局限**：传统服务栈中，分词被视为可忽略的 CPU 阶段。然而，在前缀缓存命中后，分词成为了首字延迟（TTFT）中最大的组成部分。此外，由单个 CPU 前端为整个 GPU 集群进行分词限制了系统能够服务的 GPU 数量，成为扩展瓶颈。

## 文章的核心贡献点
- **提出了 GraphTok**：一种基于 GPU 的分词器，将包括预分词、字节对编码（BPE）合并到 Token ID 组装在内的整个编码管道，作为一个可重放的 CUDA 图运行。
- **挑战1：GPU 分词的精度与兼容性难题**。在 GPU 上复现复杂的 BPE 算法并保证与参考实现比特级一致极具挑战性，且需适配多种模型架构。GraphTok 通过在 GPT-2、Llama 3、Qwen 2.5 等模型上实现比特级精确复现，并针对短输入智能回退至 CPU 引擎，解决了精度和效率平衡问题。
- **挑战2：系统集成与端到端性能瓶颈**。将分词从 CPU 移至 GPU 需无缝集成到现有服务框架中而不破坏原有优化。GraphTok 无需修改即可插件式接入 vLLM 和 NVIDIA Dynamo，通过消除 CPU-GPU 间的同步等待和数据传输瓶颈，显著降低了 TTFT 并提升了吞吐量。

## 实现与部署，evaluation 结果，要有和相关工作对比
- **实现与部署**：GraphTok 作为一个独立的 GPU 分词模块，支持无缝集成到未修改的 vLLM 和 NVIDIA Dynamo 中。它采用混合策略，长文本使用 GPU CUDA 图加速，短文本交由 CPU 处理。
- **速度对比**：在 Llama 3 上，GraphTok 比最强的 CPU 分词器 gigatoken 快 4.7-6.0 倍；在 TokTier 基准测试中，比 gigatoken 快 2.6-3.9 倍，比 TokTier 快高达 18.1 倍。编码一百万个 GPT-2 Token 仅需 1.7-3.2 毫秒（含数据传输）。
- **TTFT 优化**：在启用前缀缓存的 vLLM 中，GraphTok 将平均 TTFT 降低了 2.1-2.4 倍。
- **吞吐量与容量**：在 P99 延迟低于 2 秒的目标下，单个 Dynamo 前端配合 GraphTok 可维持 518 请求/秒（121k Token 流量），足以支撑 56 个 GPU 的繁忙小时负载；相比之下，gigatoken 仅支持 296 请求/秒，默认分词器仅支持 18.5 请求/秒。GraphTok 的负载承受能力是 gigatoken 的 1.75-2.5 倍，且在 gigatoken 尾延迟崩溃的场景下，P99 延迟低至其 1/64。

#### 总结
GraphTok 通过将分词任务卸载到 GPU 并利用 CUDA 图技术，有效解决了 Agentic 工作负载中因前缀缓存普及而凸显的分词瓶颈。它不仅大幅降低了首字延迟，更显著提升了单前端能支持的 GPU 集群规模和整体系统吞吐量，为大规模 LLM 代理服务提供了高效的基础设施支持。
items.summary_en:
## 1. What the Paper Does
- **Background**: With the rise of LLM agents, workloads involve repeated calls with long, largely unchanged contexts. While prefix caching skips most prefill computation, every request must still be fully tokenized before the cache can be queried.
- **Limitations of Existing Work**: Tokenization, historically a negligible CPU stage, has become the dominant component of Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) when prefix caching is used. Furthermore, a single CPU frontend tokenizing for an entire GPU fleet creates a scalability bottleneck, limiting the number of GPUs it can feed.

## Core Contributions
- **Proposed GraphTok**: A GPU-based tokenizer that executes the entire encoding pipeline—from pre-tokenization and Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) merging to token-ID assembly—as a single replayable CUDA graph.
- **Challenge 1: Precision and Compatibility on GPU**. Replicating complex BPE logic on GPU with bit-for-bit accuracy across diverse models is difficult. GraphTok solves this by achieving exact reference reproduction on models like Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5, while intelligently offloading short inputs to CPU where GPU offers no advantage.
- **Challenge 2: System Integration and End-to-End Latency**. Moving tokenization to GPU requires seamless integration without disrupting existing optimizations. GraphTok plugs into unmodified vLLM and NVIDIA Dynamo, eliminating CPU-GPU synchronization bottlenecks and significantly reducing TTFT.

## Implementation and Evaluation
- **Implementation**: GraphTok integrates as a plugin into standard serving stacks (vLLM, NVIDIA Dynamo) without code modifications, using a hybrid approach for input lengths.
- **Speed Comparison**: On Llama 3, GraphTok is 4.7-6.0x faster than gigatoken (the strongest CPU tokenizer). It encodes one million GPT-2 tokens in 1.7-3.2 ms including data transfers.
- **TTFT Reduction**: In vLLM with prefix caching, GraphTok reduces mean TTFT by 2.1-2.4x.
- **Throughput and Capacity**: Under a 2s P99 latency target, a single Dynamo frontend with GraphTok sustains 518 requests/s (121k-token traffic), supporting the load of 56 GPUs. In contrast, gigatoken supports only 296 requests/s, and the default tokenizer only 18.5 requests/s. GraphTok sustains 1.75-2.5x the load of gigatoken with up to 64x lower P99 latency in tail-heavy scenarios.

## 4. Conclusion
GraphTok effectively addresses the tokenization bottleneck in Agentic LLM serving by offloading the task to GPU via CUDA graphs. It significantly lowers TTFT and dramatically increases the capacity of single frontends to support large GPU clusters, providing a scalable infrastructure solution for high-throughput LLM agent applications.

items.title: Rollout-Time Intervention: Unlocking Agentic Reinforcement Learning Beyond Policy Limits
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a key paradigm for improving large language model (LLM) agents, enabling stronger reasoning, planning, and tool-use in interactive environments. However, existing agent RL methods remain fundamentally constrained by an on-policy reasoning bottleneck: when tasks exceed the model's current capability boundary, effective trajectories become extremely sparse and training often collapses. We introduce Rollout-Time Intervention (RTI), a technique designed to elicit successful trajectories beyond the policy's intrinsic exploration capacity. RTI operates by leveraging reward-side evidence (i.e., evaluation rubrics) during rollout to convert erroneous trajectories into successful ones, providing effective learning signals for tasks that the policy rarely solves on its own. Although intervention trajectories are inherently off-policy, we find that they can effectively guide policy optimization when trajectories with excessive distributional shifts are filtered out. Extensive experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate that RTI consistently outperforms RL baselines, enabling the post-trained policy to approach the performance of substantially stronger contemporary LLMs and, more importantly, transcend its original capability boundary. The code is available at https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/qqr.
items.summary_cn:
## 文章做了什么
- **背景**：强化学习（RL）已成为提升大语言模型（LLM）智能体在推理、规划和工具使用方面能力的关键范式。然而，现有的智能体 RL 方法受限于“在线策略推理瓶颈”：当任务超出模型当前的能力边界时，有效的成功轨迹变得极其稀疏，导致训练不稳定甚至崩溃。
- **已有工作的局限**：标准的在线 RL 主要放大当前策略已支持的行为，难以诱导新的推理模式。虽然教师引导方法（如 LUFFY, OPD）能部分缓解此问题，但其性能上限受限于教师模型的能力，无法帮助模型突破自身的能力边界。

## 文章的核心贡献点
- **提出了 Rollout-Time Intervention (RTI)**：一种在 rollout 阶段利用奖励侧证据（评估规则）将错误轨迹转化为成功轨迹的技术，旨在激发超出策略内在探索能力的成功路径。
- **挑战1：有效轨迹稀疏导致训练崩溃**。当任务难度超过模型能力时，模型很难自发产生成功轨迹，导致缺乏有效的学习信号。RTI 通过在 rollout 过程中介入，利用评估规则修正早期的关键错误决策，将原本失败的轨迹转化为成功的示范，从而为那些策略极少能独立解决的任务提供高质量的学习信号。
- **挑战2：干预轨迹的离线分布偏移问题**。由于干预产生的轨迹本质上属于离线数据（off-policy），直接用于训练可能导致分布偏移过大而损害策略。RTI 通过过滤掉分布偏移过大的轨迹，确保只有适度的干预数据被用于策略优化，从而在保证稳定性的同时利用这些高价值数据指导策略更新。

## 实现与部署，evaluation 结果，要有和相关工作对比
- **实验设置**：在五个基准测试上进行了广泛实验。
- **结果对比**：RTI  consistently 优于现有的 RL 基线方法。
- **性能表现**：经过 RTI 训练后的策略不仅接近了显著更强的当代 LLM 的性能水平，更重要的是，它成功超越了模型原始的能力边界，证明了该方法在解锁智能体潜力方面的有效性。

#### 总结
本文针对智能体强化学习中因任务超出能力边界导致的训练崩溃问题，提出了 Rollout-Time Intervention (RTI) 方法。通过在 rollout 阶段利用评估规则修正错误轨迹并过滤高分布偏移数据，RTI 有效解决了有效轨迹稀疏和离线数据分布偏移的挑战。实验表明，RTI 能显著提升智能体性能，使其突破原有能力限制，为提升 LLM 智能体的复杂任务处理能力提供了新途径。
items.summary_en:
## 1. What the Paper Does
- **Background**: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is a key paradigm for enhancing Large Language Model (LLM) agents in reasoning, planning, and tool use. However, existing agent RL methods suffer from an "on-policy reasoning bottleneck": when tasks exceed the model's current capability, successful trajectories become extremely sparse, causing training instability or collapse.
- **Limitations of Prior Work**: Standard on-policy RL mainly amplifies behaviors already supported by the current policy, failing to induce new reasoning patterns. While teacher-guided methods (e.g., LUFFY, OPD) offer partial mitigation, their performance is capped by the teacher's capabilities and cannot help the model transcend its own boundaries.

## Core Contributions
- **Proposed Rollout-Time Intervention (RTI)**: A technique that leverages reward-side evidence (evaluation rubrics) during rollout to convert erroneous trajectories into successful ones, eliciting paths beyond the policy's intrinsic exploration capacity.
- **Challenge 1: Sparse Effective Trajectories Leading to Training Collapse**. When tasks are too difficult, the model rarely generates successful trajectories, starving the learning process. RTI addresses this by intervening during rollout to correct early critical errors using evaluation rules, transforming failed attempts into successful demonstrations and providing high-quality learning signals for hard tasks.
- **Challenge 2: Distributional Shift from Off-Policy Interventions**. Intervention-generated trajectories are inherently off-policy, risking performance degradation due to large distributional shifts. RTI mitigates this by filtering out trajectories with excessive distributional shifts, ensuring that only moderately shifted, high-value data guides policy optimization safely.

## Implementation and Evaluation
- **Experimental Setup**: Extensive experiments were conducted across five benchmarks.
- **Results**: RTI consistently outperforms existing RL baselines.
- **Performance**: The post-trained policy not only approaches the performance of significantly stronger contemporary LLMs but, more importantly, transcends its original capability boundary, demonstrating the method's effectiveness in unlocking agent potential.

## 4. Conclusion
This paper addresses the training collapse in agent RL caused by tasks exceeding model capabilities by proposing Rollout-Time Intervention (RTI). By correcting erroneous trajectories during rollout using evaluation rules and filtering for distributional shift, RTI effectively tackles the challenges of trajectory sparsity and off-policy data usage. Experiments show that RTI significantly enhances agent performance, allowing it to surpass original capability limits, offering a new pathway for improving LLM agents in complex tasks.

items.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
items.abstract: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment. Unlike systems that optimize the entire ML script or search architectures in a discrete space, the framework operates over an open but semantically narrow space: the agent generates code only for the specified components, leaving the overall network structure unchanged. The approach is validated in two directions: tuning a classification spiking neural network with correlation learning, and solving high-order differential equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). Across five tasks---spiking classification on MNIST and Digits, and boundary-value problems for the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) equations---the agent outperforms the baselines: classification accuracy is 13 percentage points (MNIST) and 6 percentage points (Digits) higher; the error against the analytical single-soliton solution is reduced approximately 2491-fold; the invariant-preservation error drops approximately 325-fold in the selected GNLSE run with a Gaussian perturbation and by more than 100-fold on average over repeated initializations; and the mass drift drops 14-fold for the KS problem with a Gaussian perturbation. The framework thus tunes key components on tasks of different nature without changing its internal structure.

items.summary_cn:
## 文章做了什么
- **背景**：许多机器学习方法采用双层结构，专家首先选择方法类别，随后关键组件的选择至关重要但通常依赖人工手动调整。这种手动过程劳动密集且难以复现。
- **已有工作为什么解决不了**：现有的自动化系统要么优化整个机器学习脚本，要么在离散空间中搜索网络架构。这些方法缺乏灵活性或计算成本过高，无法针对特定模型的关键功能模块进行精细、语义受限的自动调优，且难以在不同性质的模型间通用。

## 文章的核心贡献点
- **提出了一个多代理大语言模型（LLM）框架**：该框架包含分析师、编码器和记录员三个角色，配合实验日志和沙盒执行环境，用于自动调整专用神经网络的关键组件。
- **挑战1：如何在保持整体网络结构不变的情况下，精准生成特定组件的代码？**
  - **难点**：直接生成完整脚本容易引入错误且难以控制，而传统架构搜索空间过大。
  - **解决方案**：框架在一个开放但语义狭窄的空间中操作，代理仅生成指定组件（如输入编码、损失函数项）的代码，保留整体网络结构不变，从而降低搜索复杂度并提高代码准确性。
- **挑战2：如何实现框架在不同性质任务间的通用性和可迁移性？**
  - **难点**：脉冲神经网络（SNN）和物理信息神经网络（PINN）等领域差异巨大，缺乏统一的调优规则。
  - **解决方案**：通过将不同模型分解为相似的模块（输入预处理、特征变换、解码/输出变换、损失函数），利用多代理协作机制统一处理这些模块的调优，验证了其在分类任务和微分方程求解任务中的跨领域迁移能力。

## 实现与部署，evaluation 结果，要有和相关工作对比
- **实现与部署**：系统由三个LLM代理角色组成，集成沙盒执行环境以安全运行生成的代码，并通过实验日志积累历史经验。详细设计的提示词显著提升了性能较弱的LLM的表现。
- **评估结果**：在五个任务上进行了验证，包括MNIST和Digits数据集上的脉冲分类，以及广义非线性薛定谔方程（GNLSE）和Kuramoto–Sivashinsky（KS）方程的边值问题。
- **对比优势**：
  - **分类任务**：相比基线方法，MNIST分类准确率提高了13个百分点，Digits提高了6个百分点。
  - **物理方程求解**：在GNLSE任务中，相对于解析单孤子解的误差减少了约2491倍；在高斯扰动下，不变量保持误差减少了约325倍，平均重复初始化下减少超过100倍。在KS问题中，质量漂移减少了14倍。
  - **结论**：该框架在不改变内部结构的情况下，显著优于传统基线方法，证明了其在不同性质任务中调优关键组件的有效性。

#### 总结
本文提出了一种基于多代理LLM的自动化调优框架，专门用于调整专用神经网络模型中的关键功能模块。通过限制代码生成范围至特定组件并保持整体架构稳定，该方法成功克服了传统自动化ML方法在灵活性和通用性上的局限。实验结果表明，该框架在脉冲神经网络分类和物理信息神经网络求解微分方程等截然不同的任务中均取得了显著的性能提升，展现了强大的跨领域迁移能力和自动化调优潜力。
items.summary_en:
## 1. What the Paper Did
- **Background**: Many machine learning approaches follow a two-level structure where experts select a method class, but the critical choice of key components within that class is usually manual. This manual process is labor-intensive and poorly reproducible.
- **Why Existing Work Falls Short**: Existing automated systems either optimize entire ML scripts or search for architectures in discrete spaces. These approaches lack the flexibility to finely tune specific functional modules within a fixed architecture or are computationally prohibitive, failing to provide a generalizable solution for specialized models like Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) or Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs).

## Core Contributions
- **Proposed a Multi-Agent LLM Framework**: The system features three roles—analyst, coder, and recorder—integrated with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment to automate the tuning of key neural network components.
- **Challenge 1: How to precisely generate code for specific components while keeping the overall network structure unchanged?**
  - **Difficulty**: Generating full scripts is error-prone and hard to control, while traditional architecture search spaces are too vast.
  - **Solution**: The framework operates in an open but semantically narrow space, where agents generate code only for specified components (e.g., input encoding, loss terms), leaving the main network structure intact. This reduces search complexity and improves code accuracy.
- **Challenge 2: How to achieve generalizability and transferability across tasks of different natures?**
  - **Difficulty**: Domains like SNNs and PINNs differ significantly, lacking universal tuning rules.
  - **Solution**: By decomposing diverse models into similar modules (input preprocessing, feature transformation, decoding/output, loss function), the multi-agent collaboration mechanism uniformly handles module tuning, demonstrating cross-domain transferability in both classification and differential equation solving tasks.

## Implementation and Evaluation
- **Implementation**: The system comprises three LLM agent roles, integrates a sandboxed environment for safe code execution, and uses experiment logs to accumulate historical experience. Detailed prompts significantly enhanced the performance of less capable LLMs.
- **Evaluation**: Validated on five tasks: spiking classification on MNIST and Digits, and boundary-value problems for the Generalized Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation (GNLSE) and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky (KS) equations.
- **Comparison with Baselines**:
  - **Classification**: Accuracy improved by 13 percentage points on MNIST and 6 percentage points on Digits compared to baselines.
  - **Physics Equations**: Error against the analytical single-soliton solution in GNLSE was reduced approximately 2491-fold. Invariant-preservation error dropped ~325-fold with Gaussian perturbation and >100-fold on average. Mass drift in the KS problem decreased 14-fold.
  - **Conclusion**: The framework significantly outperforms traditional baselines without altering its internal structure, proving its effectiveness in tuning key components across diverse tasks.

#### Summary
This paper proposes a multi-agent LLM-based automated tuning framework specifically designed for adjusting key functional modules in specialized neural network models. By restricting code generation to specific components while maintaining a stable overall architecture, the method overcomes the flexibility and generalizability limitations of traditional AutoML approaches. Experimental results demonstrate significant performance improvements in both Spiking Neural Network classification and Physics-Informed Neural Network differential equation solving, highlighting the framework's strong cross-domain transferability and potential for automated hyperparameter and component optimization.

本文提出了一种基于多代理LLM的自动化调优框架，专门用于调整专用神经网络模型中的关键功能模块。通过限制代码生成范围至特定组件并保持整体架构稳定，该方法成功克服了传统自动化ML方法在灵活性和通用性上的局限。实验结果表明，该框架在脉冲神经网络分类和物理信息神经网络求解微分方程等截然不同的任务中均取得了显著的性能提升，展现了强大的跨领域迁移能力和自动化调优潜力。

Institution: National Research Centre “Kurchatov Institute”, National Research Nuclear University MEPhI, Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology
This paper proposes a multi-agent LLM-based automated tuning framework specifically designed for adjusting key functional modules in specialized neural network models. By restricting code generation to specific components while maintaining a stable overall architecture, the method overcomes the flexibility and generalizability limitations of traditional AutoML approaches. Experimental results demonstrate significant performance improvements in both Spiking Neural Network classification and Physics-Informed Neural Network differential equation solving, highlighting the framework's strong cross-domain transferability and potential for automated hyperparameter and component optimization.

items.title: Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
items.abstract: Training long-horizon language model agents requires assigning credit to intermediate decisions from sparse terminal feedback. Within a finite group of sibling rollouts, useful action comparisons depend on their context, evidence for both alternatives, and how that evidence enters learning. We propose Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization (MCGPO), a procedure for constructing weighted action preferences from already collected trajectories. MCGPO defines comparison contexts with pre-action state summaries and observed rubric progress, annotated by task rules. Two-action support selects among ordered exact and coarse matching rules. Fixed folds separate candidate decisions from the terminal outcomes used to orient their preferences, and support-dependent evidence weights scale an auxiliary pairwise objective alongside shared GraphGPO task learning. MCGPO reuses rollout data and each response's original history, preserving critic-free training. Across six environment-backbone settings with three training seeds each, MCGPO improves mean success over matched GraphGPO: by 0.47-1.46 percentage points on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B, and by 3.96 and 5.16 points on WebShop with Qwen3-4B and 8B. The ALFWorld gains build on baseline success above 92%, where remaining headroom is limited. Integrated success improves in three of four Qwen2.5 settings. Three-seed factorial controls support opposite-fold evidence and evidence weighting; joint state-rubric matching achieves the highest mean in all four representation-control settings.
items.institution: Imperial College London, University of Science and Technology of China, Meituan, Tsinghua University
items.summary_cn:
## 文章做了什么
- **背景**：训练长视野语言模型智能体（LLM Agents）需要从稀疏的终端反馈中为中间决策分配信用。现有的组相对强化学习（Group-relative RL）方法通过比较一组采样响应或轨迹的结果来进行无评论家（critic-free）更新。
- **已有工作的局限**：现有的方法（如 GiGPO 或基于轨迹图的方法）通常仅根据重复的状态或转换来分组决策。然而，相同的状态摘要可能对应任务的不同阶段（例如，相同的柜台状态可能出现在获取目标物体之前或之后）。这种“上下文不匹配”导致比较混合了先前的任务进度和当前动作的贡献，使得信用分配不准确。虽然增加上下文可以区分这些决策，但更严格的条件会减少可用于比较不同动作的证据数量。

## 文章的核心贡献点
- **提出了一个 Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization (MCGPO)**：一种从已收集的轨迹中构建加权动作偏好的过程，通过定义包含预动作状态摘要和观察到的规则进度的比较上下文来解决信用分配问题。
- **挑战1：上下文不匹配导致的信用分配噪声**。难点在于相同的状态摘要可能掩盖了不同的前置任务进度，导致动作对比失真。MCGPO 通过引入由任务规则注释的“观察到的规则进度”（observed rubric progress）与状态摘要共同定义比较上下文，确保只有处于相同任务进展阶段的决策才会被相互比较。
- **挑战2：严格匹配导致的证据稀疏性**。难点在于如果匹配条件过于严格，每组内可比较的动作对数量会急剧减少，影响学习效率。MCGPO 设计了双动作支持机制（Two-action support），在有序精确匹配和粗略匹配规则之间进行选择，并利用依赖于支持的证据权重（support-dependent evidence weights）来缩放辅助成对目标，从而在保持匹配质量的同时充分利用数据。

## 实现与部署，evaluation 结果，要有和相关工作对比
- **实现细节**：MCGPO 重用 rollout 数据和每个响应的原始历史，保持了无评论家训练的特性。它使用固定折叠（Fixed folds）将候选决策与用于确定其偏好方向的终端结果分离开来。
- **实验结果**：在六个环境-骨干网络设置中（每个设置三个训练种子），MCGPO 相比匹配的 GraphGPO 基线取得了显著提升：
    - 在 ALFWorld 和 WebShop 上，使用 Qwen2.5-1.5B 和 7B 模型时，平均成功率提高了 0.47-1.46 个百分点。
    - 在 WebShop 上，使用 Qwen3-4B 和 8B 模型时，成功率分别提高了 3.96 和 5.16 个百分点。
    - 值得注意的是，ALFWorld 的提升是在基线成功率已超过 92% 的情况下取得的，剩余提升空间有限。
- **对比分析**：消融实验表明，联合状态-规则匹配（joint state-rubric matching）在所有四种表示控制设置中均取得了最高的平均成功率，证明了结合状态和规则进度的有效性。相比之下，单纯的相反折叠证据或证据加权效果不如联合匹配。

#### 总结
本文针对 LLM 智能体训练中的长视野信用分配问题，提出了 MCGPO 方法。通过引入规则感知的上下文匹配机制，解决了传统组相对 RL 方法中因状态摘要模糊导致的上下文不匹配问题。实验证明，MCGPO 在多个基准测试和模型规模上均优于现有的 GraphGPO 方法，特别是在高基线性能下仍能实现显著增益，为无评论家的 LLM 智能体训练提供了更精细的信用分配方案。
items.summary_en:
## 1. What the Paper Does
- **Background**: Training long-horizon LLM agents requires assigning credit to intermediate decisions from sparse terminal feedback. Existing group-relative reinforcement learning methods perform critic-free updates by comparing outcomes within groups of sampled responses or trajectories.
- **Limitations of Prior Work**: Current methods (e.g., GiGPO, trajectory-graph methods) typically group decisions based solely on repeated states or transitions. However, identical state summaries can correspond to different stages of task progress (e.g., visiting a countertop before or after acquiring an object). This "context mismatch" causes action comparisons to conflate prior progress with the current action's contribution, leading to inaccurate credit assignment. While adding context can distinguish these decisions, stricter conditions reduce the amount of evidence available for comparison.

## Core Contributions
- **Proposed Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization (MCGPO)**: A procedure for constructing weighted action preferences from collected trajectories by defining comparison contexts that include pre-action state summaries and observed rubric progress.
- **Challenge 1: Noisy credit assignment due to context mismatch**. The difficulty lies in identical state summaries obscuring different prior task progresses, distorting action comparisons. MCGPO addresses this by defining comparison contexts using both state summaries and "observed rubric progress" annotated by task rules, ensuring only decisions at similar task stages are compared.
- **Challenge 2: Data sparsity caused by strict matching**. The difficulty is that overly strict matching conditions drastically reduce the number of comparable action pairs per group, hindering learning efficiency. MCGPO employs a "Two-action support" mechanism that selects between ordered exact and coarse matching rules, using support-dependent evidence weights to scale the auxiliary pairwise objective, thereby balancing match quality with data utilization.

## Implementation and Evaluation
- **Implementation**: MCGPO reuses rollout data and original response histories, maintaining critic-free training. It uses fixed folds to separate candidate decisions from the terminal outcomes used to orient preferences.
- **Results**: Across six environment-backbone settings (with three seeds each), MCGPO significantly outperforms the matched GraphGPO baseline:
    - On ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B, mean success rates improved by 0.47–1.46 percentage points.
    - On WebShop with Qwen3-4B and 8B, success rates improved by 3.96 and 5.16 points, respectively.
    - Notably, gains on ALFWorld were achieved despite a baseline success rate already exceeding 92%, indicating effectiveness even with limited headroom.
- **Comparison**: Ablation studies showed that joint state-rubric matching achieved the highest mean success in all four representation-control settings, outperforming methods using only opposite-fold evidence or evidence weighting, thus validating the efficacy of combining state and rule progress.

## 4. Conclusion
This paper addresses the long-horizon credit assignment problem in LLM agent training by proposing MCGPO. By introducing a rule-aware context matching mechanism, it resolves the context mismatch issue inherent in traditional group-relative RL methods. Experiments demonstrate that MCGPO surpasses existing GraphGPO methods across multiple benchmarks and model scales, achieving significant gains even in high-performance regimes, offering a more refined credit assignment solution for critic-free LLM agent training.

items.title: AgentTune: A Unified Training Lifecycle for Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.abstract: Tool-using agents increasingly require a common substrate for building, training, evaluating, distilling, and maintaining agentic systems, yet existing tooling typically addresses these stages in isolation. We present AgentTune, a source-available Python library that provides a unified framework for developing and optimizing tool-using agents. At its core, AgentTune introduces a two-tier EventLog representation that preserves agent trajectories while supporting consistent projections for training, evaluation, and auditing. Building on this substrate, the library provides a shared agent runtime, tool-calling reinforcement learning, agentic distillation, retrieval-augmented generation, decision workflows, evaluation utilities, and a designed path toward self-healing agents. These components are exposed through composable interfaces so that agent strategies, training methods, evaluation procedures, and recovery mechanisms can be combined without requiring separate representations or pipelines. We demonstrate the framework across agentic tasks including legal contract search and domain-specific applications, illustrating its use for trajectory-based optimization, tool-use evaluation, and cross-task agent development. AgentTune is released as a source-available library at https://github.com/Lexsi-Labs/AgentTune
items.summary_cn:
## 文章做了什么
- **背景**：随着使用工具的 LLM Agent 日益复杂，构建、训练、评估、蒸馏和维护这些系统需要一个共同的基础设施。然而，现有的工具通常孤立地处理这些阶段。
- **已有工作为什么解决不了**：现有工具如 TRL、verl 用于训练策略，LangGraph 用于编排状态循环，lm-eval 用于静态评估，它们在接口上是碎片化的。RL rollout、决策工作流状态和评估追踪使用不同的数据表示，导致评分、损失掩码、失败检测和审计逻辑需要在不同阶段重复重建，缺乏统一的数据底层。

## 文章的核心贡献点
- **提出了一个 AgentTune 框架**：这是一个开源的 Python 库，为开发和使用工具的 Agent 提供统一的框架，核心是两层 EventLog 表示法。
- **挑战1：数据表示的碎片化与不一致性**。不同阶段（训练、评估、审计）需要不同的数据格式，导致 pipeline 割难且难以维护。AgentTune 通过引入两层 EventLog 表示法，一次性记录 Agent 交互轨迹，并支持向训练（SFT行）、评估输入和审计记录的一致投影，解决了数据孤岛问题。
- **挑战2：训练与恢复机制的孤立**。传统的强化学习和蒸馏方法往往独立于执行环境，难以利用实时反馈进行自我修复或优化。AgentTune 提供了共享的 Agent 运行时和基于 TRL 的 RL 核心，支持 GRPO、PPO 等多种算法，并将检测到的失败转化为纠正性训练数据，实现了从执行到自我修复的闭环。

## 实现与部署，evaluation 结果，要有和相关工作对比
- **实现与部署**：AgentTune 作为一个源可用（source-available）库发布，提供了可组合的接口，允许用户自由组合 Agent 策略、训练方法、评估程序和恢复机制。它集成了工具调用强化学习、Agent 蒸馏、检索增强生成（RAG）和决策工作流。
- **评估结果**：文章在法律合同搜索等特定领域任务中展示了该框架的有效性。通过在一个合成的问题集上训练搜索 Agent，并在三个未见过的语料库上进行评估，证明了其在基于轨迹的优化和工具使用评估方面的能力。
- **对比**：与仅关注微调方法的 AgentTuning 不同，AgentTune 是一个完整的软件库，涵盖了从数据收集到恢复的全生命周期。相较于孤立的 TRL 或 LangGraph，AgentTune 消除了中间数据转换的需要，提高了开发效率和系统的一致性。

#### 总结
AgentTune 通过定义统一的轨迹契约（EventLog）和共享的训练栈，解决了当前 LLM Agent 开发中工具链碎片化的问题。它不仅简化了从构建到维护的开发流程，还通过支持自我修复和多种强化学习算法，提升了 Agent 的鲁棒性和性能。该框架为未来复杂 Agent 系统的标准化开发和优化提供了重要基础。
items.summary_en:
## 1. What the Paper Does
- **Background**: Tool-using LLM agents increasingly require a common substrate for building, training, evaluating, distilling, and maintaining agentic systems.
- **Why Existing Work Falls Short**: Existing tools (e.g., TRL, LangGraph, lm-eval) address these stages in isolation with fragmented interfaces. Different representations for RL rollouts, decision workflows, and evaluation traces force developers to repeatedly reconstruct logic for scoring, loss masking, and auditing, leading to inefficiency and inconsistency.

## Core Contributions
- **Proposed AgentTune Framework**: A source-available Python library providing a unified framework for developing and optimizing tool-using agents, centered around a two-tier EventLog representation.
- **Challenge 1: Fragmented Data Representations**. Different lifecycle stages require disparate data formats, creating silos. AgentTune solves this by introducing a two-tier EventLog that records agent interactions once and supports consistent projections for training (SFT rows), evaluation inputs, and audit records.
- **Challenge 2: Isolated Training and Recovery Mechanisms**. Traditional RL and distillation are often disconnected from execution environments. AgentTune provides a shared agent runtime and TRL-backed RL core supporting various algorithms (GRPO, PPO, etc.), enabling the conversion of detected failures into corrective training data for self-healing capabilities.

## Implementation and Evaluation
- **Implementation**: Released as a source-available library with composable interfaces. It integrates tool-calling reinforcement learning, agentic distillation, RAG, and decision workflows, allowing flexible combination of strategies without separate pipelines.
- **Evaluation Results**: Demonstrated on agentic tasks such as legal contract search. A search agent trained on synthesized questions was evaluated on three unseen corpora, illustrating effective trajectory-based optimization and tool-use evaluation.
- **Comparison**: Unlike AgentTuning (a method/dataset), AgentTune is a comprehensive software library covering the full lifecycle. Compared to isolated tools like TRL or LangGraph, it eliminates intermediate data conversion overhead, enhancing development efficiency and system consistency.

## 4. Conclusion
AgentTune addresses the fragmentation in LLM agent toolchains by defining a unified trajectory contract (EventLog) and a shared training stack. It simplifies the development lifecycle from build to maintenance and enhances agent robustness through self-healing and diverse RL support, providing a foundational framework for standardized complex agent system development.
